title: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation

paper.title: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation
paper.abstract: Abstract Recent diffusion models have achieved impressive progress in single image to multi-view generation by synthesizing consistent novel views efficiently. Existing methods usually explicitly or implicitly couple geometry inference and texture synthesis, making generation vulnerable to inaccurate geometry prediction. Although several geometry-guided methods have explored decoupling, they usually treat predicted geometry as a fixed condition and do not explicitly model whether the geometry is reliable. We therefore propose Reliability-Guided Multi-View Generation (RGMV), which comprises a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) and a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module. Specifically, a geometry proposal generator produces multiple geometry predictions for the same reference image and target viewpoints under different stochastic sampling configurations. SCG measures their spatial agreement to derive a reliability map, which RGI uses to modulate the injection strength of geometry-conditioned residuals in the RGB synthesis model. Moreover, RGMV can adapt to different geometry proposal generators. As a result, RGMV preserves stronger geometric guidance in stable regions while attenuating unreliable geometry cues before they propagate into multi-view RGB generation. Extensive experiments show that reliability-aware geometry injection improves the geometric quality of multi-view generation. Code: https://github.com/WISLab-GDUT/RGMV .

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Multi-view Consistent Image Generation aims to synthesize visually coherent images of an object from novel viewpoints given only one reference image. Recent diffusion-based approaches have substantially improved the realism and efficiency of multi-view synthesis [ 39 , 33 , 31 , 8 , 29 , 27 , 43 , 25 , 4 , 7 ] by leveraging large-scale image priors and joint view generation [ 37 , 28 , 21 , 38 , 16 , 44 ] . Nevertheless, a single reference image provides only partial observations of the underlying object. The geometry of occluded and unseen regions therefore remains underconstrained, making it difficult to preserve plausible object structure and multi-view consistent local appearance. To reduce this ambiguity, geometry-guided methods [ 19 , 20 , 26 , 15 , 6 , 13 , 42 ] introduce normal maps, depth maps, or other structural representations as explicit conditions for multi-view RGB synthesis. When the geometry condition is accurate, it provides view-aware structural cues that help constrain object shape and appearance in unseen regions. Figure 1 (a,b) highlights two alternative formulations for multi-view generation. Direct methods do not expose geometry as an independently controllable signal, whereas geometry-guided pipelines expose it without accounting for its non-uniform reliability. However, geometry predicted from a single reference image is not uniformly reliable. Ambiguity in occluded regions, thin structures, and local boundaries can lead to spatially and view-wise varying errors in the predicted geometry. Existing geometry-conditioned pipelines [ 45 , 25 , 19 , 20 , 26 ] typically inject predicted geometry with a globally fixed strength, implicitly treating all geometric cues as equally trustworthy. This design creates an unavoidable trade-off that weak conditioning underuses reliable geometry, whereas strong conditioning propagates local geometric errors into RGB synthesis. Because the reliability of predicted geometry varies across spatial locations and target views, no single global injection scale can simultaneously preserve trustworthy structural cues and suppress unreliable ones. This limitation motivates a selective geometry-conditioning mechanism that preserves stable geometric cues while suppressing unreliable ones. Figure 1 : Comparison of three paradigms for multi-view image generation. (a) Direct generation entangles geometric reasoning and texture synthesis in a single generator, making geometric errors difficult to isolate. (b) Geometry-guided generation separates geometry prediction from RGB synthesis, but applies predicted geometry with spatially uniform influence. (c) RGMV conditions RGB synthesis on an anchor geometry prediction and uses per-view spatial reliability maps estimated by SCG to modulate geometry residuals through RGI. Therefore, we propose RGMV, a reliability-guided framework for geometry-guided multi-view generation. Figure 1 (c) summarizes the resulting alternative. RGMV retains the decoupled pipeline but selectively controls the influence of predicted geometry rather than modifying the geometry itself. RGMV obtains multiple normal predictions for the same reference image and target poses from a geometry proposal generator under different stochastic seeds. SCG converts their agreement into spatial reliability maps, and RGI uses these maps to modulate the geometry residuals injected into the multi-view RGB synthesis model. This design preserves stronger geometry guidance in stable regions while limiting the influence of inconsistent predictions. Experiments show that SCG-guided RGI improves over spatially uniform injection with a frozen RGB synthesis model, and parameter-efficient adaptation further improves the full RGMV framework. The main contributions of this work are as follows: • We propose RGMV, which couples a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) for estimating spatial reliability from stochastic geometry agreement with a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module for modulating normal-conditioned residuals. • We introduce a parameter-efficient adaptation scheme for the RGI-equipped RGB synthesis model, which uses ground-truth normals during training and SCG-derived spatial variation only at inference, without dependence on a particular geometry proposal generator. • Extensive experiments on Objaverse and GSO demonstrate that RGMV consistently improves multiple geometry proposal generators in both multi-view RGB synthesis and downstream 3D reconstruction. Qualitative results show more stable structures on rendered objects and real captured images.

sections.heading: 2.1 Multi-view Consistent Image Generation
sections.text: Diffusion-based models [ 17 , 32 , 18 , 33 , 36 , 35 ] have become a major approach for synthesizing novel views from a single reference image. Zero-1-to-3 [ 17 ] introduces camera-conditioned diffusion, enabling novel-view generation under specified relative camera transformations. SyncDreamer [ 18 ] further models the joint distribution of multiple target views and synchronizes their denoising process through cross-view feature interaction to improve multi-view consistency. SV3D [ 36 ] adapts latent video diffusion to orbital multi-view synthesis and incorporates explicit camera control for image-conditioned view generation. Era3D [ 14 ] improves high-resolution multi-view generation through camera prediction and efficient row-wise attention that exploits epipolar correspondence across views. More recently, MV-Adapter [ 10 ] introduces a lightweight adapter-based design that equips pretrained text-to-image diffusion models with multi-view generation capability while preserving the original backbone. These methods [ 35 , 34 , 47 , 7 , 1 ] improve the realism, camera controllability, and cross-view coherence of image-based multi-view synthesis. Their primary focus is on constructing stronger multi-view generation priors or more effective cross-view interactions. In this work, we study how external geometry predicted from a single reference image should be used within an existing multi-view diffusion pipeline when the reliability varies across spatial regions and target views.

sections.heading: 2.2 Geometry-conditioned Diffusion Models
sections.text: Geometry conditions have been widely used to provide explicit spatial control for diffusion models [ 45 , 25 , 43 , 9 , 22 , 40 , 24 , 2 ] . ControlNet [ 45 ] introduces an additional trainable branch that injects spatial conditions, such as edges, depth maps, and normal maps, into a pretrained diffusion backbone. T2I-Adapter [ 25 ] instead learns lightweight adapters for external structural signals while keeping the original text-to-image model frozen. These methods establish effective mechanisms for incorporating geometry into image diffusion. Several works further incorporate geometry into multi-view or 3D generation [ 19 , 20 , 6 , 13 , 15 ] . Wonder3D [ 19 ] jointly generates multi-view RGB images and normal maps through cross-domain diffusion and multi-view cross-domain attention. Direct2.5 [ 20 ] models multi-view normal maps as a 2.5D representation and uses normal-conditioned multi-view image generation for appearance synthesis. PointmapDiff [ 26 ] uses predicted pointmaps as geometric conditions for single-image novel-view synthesis through reference attention and ControlNet-based conditioning. In a related texture-generation setting, CaliTex [ 15 ] calibrates attention with known 3D structure to improve view-coherent texture synthesis. These methods demonstrate that explicit geometry can substantially improve view synthesis and appearance generation. However, they generally use the available geometric representation directly or condition generation with a globally fixed mechanism [ 45 , 19 , 20 , 26 ] . Regarding this issue, RGMV uses multi-sample agreement to adapt the strength of geometry-conditioned residual injection at inference time.

sections.heading: 2.3 Consistency-based Reliability Estimation
sections.text: Multi-sample consistency has been explored as an inference-time signal for assessing the reliability of generative outputs [ 23 , 12 , 11 ] . Generative Uncertainty in Diffusion Models [ 12 ] estimates the uncertainty of diffusion samples to identify potentially low-quality generations. Self-Refining Video Sampling [ 11 ] uses self-consistency to identify regions that benefit from selective refinement during video generation. These studies show that repeated stochastic generations can provide useful evidence about output stability without requiring an additional manually annotated reliability label. RGMV evaluates the stability of the geometry condition before it is injected into downstream multi-view RGB synthesis. Specifically, SCG measures agreement among normal predictions generated under different stochastic seeds and converts it into a spatial reliability map. This parameter-free signal directly modulates normal-conditioned residuals at inference time, allowing the multi-view diffusion model to retain stable geometric cues while attenuating geometry conditions that are locally inconsistent. Figure 2 : Overview of RGMV. Given a reference image and target camera poses, an off-the-shelf geometry proposal generator produces K K stochastic sets of multi-view normal predictions. The first prediction set serves as the anchor normal condition to produce multi-level geometry residuals. In parallel, Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) in (a) groups normal predictions by target view, measures their per-pixel angular disagreement, and converts it into per-view spatial reliability maps. Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module in (b) resizes and affinely calibrates the corresponding reliability map at each denoising level l l to obtain 𝐑 ~ v , l \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}_{v,l} , which selectively modulates the geometry residual before it is injected into the multi-view diffusion backbone.

sections.heading: 3.3 Reliability-aware Geometry Injection
sections.text: The proposed RGI module (Fig. 2 (b)) injects geometry into the denoising network of the RGB synthesis model through residuals produced by a normal-conditioned ControlNet [ 45 ] . sections.heading: 4.1 Dataset and Metric
sections.text: We train RGMV on a curated Objaverse [ 3 ] subset of approximately 100 100 K objects, with more than 60 60 K for training and the remainder for validation. Ablations use a fixed 100 100 -object validation subset, and the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) [ 5 ] provides a fixed 100 100 -object test set. Both of them are selected with seed 42 42 . For 2D synthesis, we report PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS [ 46 ] , which measure pixel fidelity, structural similarity, and perceptual similarity respectively. For 3D reconstruction, lower Chamfer Distance (CD) and higher Volume IoU indicate better geometric quality.

sections.heading: 4.2 Implementation Details
sections.text: Our multi-view RGB synthesis model is built on Stable Diffusion v2.1-base [ 30 ] . We use MV-Adapter [ 10 ] as the multi-view consistency module and a normal-conditioned ControlNet [ 45 ] for geometry residual injection. We use K = 3 K=3 , γ = 0.20 \gamma=0.20 , α scg = 0.08 \alpha_{\mathrm{scg}}=0.08 , and [ r min , r max ] = [ 0 , 1 ] [r_{\min},r_{\max}]=[0,1] , selected in Sec. 4.4 . During training, we optimize only the parameters of MV-Adapter for 120,000 120{,}000 steps with batch size 3 3 and learning rate 1 × 10 − 5 1\times 10^{-5} , while freezing the diffusion backbone and ControlNet, and the Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) scale is 3.0 3.0 . For each reference image, the proposal generator produces K K stochastic sets of six-view normal maps, and RGMV synthesizes the corresponding RGB views at 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} (front), 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} (front-right), 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} (right), 180 ∘ 180^{\circ} (back), 270 ∘ 270^{\circ} (left), and 315 ∘ 315^{\circ} (front-left). SCG assumes no specific camera angles, but arbitrary or continuous pose evaluation is beyond the scope of this work. Peak GPU memory is approximately 45 GB for training. Unless specified otherwise, the default geometry proposal generator of RGMV is a separately trained MV-Adapter for multi-view normal generation, trained with the same optimization settings and parameter-efficient adaptation strategy as the RGB synthesis model.

sections.heading: 4.3 Performance Comparison
sections.text: Compared Methods. We compare RGMV with two representative multi-view image generation baselines, Zero-1-to-3 [ 17 ] and SyncDreamer [ 18 ] , as well as three recent systems with distinct multi-view generation designs, including Wonder3D++ [ 41 ] , MV-Adapter [ 10 ] , and Era3D [ 14 ] . Zero-1-to-3 performs camera-conditioned novel-view synthesis from a single reference image, whereas SyncDreamer [ 18 ] explicitly models the joint distribution of multiple target views. Wonder3D++ [ 41 ] , MV-Adapter, and Era3D [ 14 ] represent complementary approaches based on joint RGB–geometry generation, lightweight multi-view adaptation, and epipolar-aware multi-view generation, respectively. The latter three methods can additionally provide multi-view geometry proposals for RGMV. We therefore evaluate each of them both as a standalone multi-view generation method and as a geometry proposal generator integrated with RGMV. sections.heading: 4.4 Ablation Study
sections.text: We conduct controlled ablations on the fixed 100 100 -object Objaverse [ 3 ] validation subset to isolate the effects of predicted-normal conditioning, SCG-guided reliability-aware geometry injection, and RGB synthesis model adaptation. All geometry-conditioned variants use multi-view normal proposals from our separately trained MV-Adapter. The “Pure i2mv” row in Table 3 corresponds to the image-only MV-Adapter RGB synthesis model and is evaluated without normal-conditioned residual injection. All geometry-conditioned variants retain the same MV-Adapter RGB backbone and are evaluated under the same reference images, target viewpoints, and generation protocol. Because RGI operationalizes the spatial reliability maps estimated by SCG, we evaluate their joint contribution by replacing the SCG-derived spatial gate with uniform injection rather than treating RGI as a separately removable component. sections.heading: 5 Conclusion
sections.text: In this paper, we presented RGMV, a reliability-guided framework for multi-view image generation. RGMV considers geometry predicted from a single reference image useful but not uniformly reliable across spatial regions and target views. The proposed SCG is parameter-free and operates at inference time to construct a reliability map from the agreement among multiple stochastic geometry predictions, while RGI uses this map to selectively modulate geometry residuals during RGB synthesis. Experiments demonstrate that RGMV improves multiple geometry proposal generators on both multi-view image synthesis and downstream 3D reconstruction. Qualitative results further show that reliability-guided conditioning reduces geometry-related artifacts and produces more stable object structures across viewpoints.

Affiliation: Guangdong University of Technology, China Jiajie Lin Affiliation: Hiroshima University, Japan Yi Yu Affiliation: Hiroshima University, Japan Zhenguo Yang Affiliation: Guangdong University of Technology, China Abstract Recent diffusion models have achieved impressive progress in single image to multi-view generation by synthesizing consistent novel views efficiently. Existing methods usually explicitly or implicitly couple geometry inference and texture synthesis, making generation vulnerable to inaccurate geometry prediction. Although several geometry-guided methods have explored decoupling, they usually treat predicted geometry as a fixed condition and do not explicitly model whether the geometry is reliable. We therefore propose Reliability-Guided Multi-View Generation (RGMV), which comprises a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) and a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module. Specifically, a geometry proposal generator produces multiple geometry predictions for the same reference image and target viewpoints under different stochastic sampling configurations. SCG measures their spatial agreement to derive a reliability map, which RGI uses to modulate the injection strength of geometry-conditioned residuals in the RGB synthesis model. Moreover, RGMV can adapt to different geometry proposal generators. As a result, RGMV preserves stronger geometric guidance in stable regions while attenuating unreliable geometry cues before they propagate into multi-view RGB generation. Extensive experiments show that reliability-aware geometry injection improves the geometric quality of multi-view generation. Code: https://github.com/WISLab-GDUT/RGMV . Keywords: Multi-view image generation Geometry-conditioned diffusion Self-consistency reliability estimation 1 Introduction Multi-view Consistent Image Generation aims to synthesize visually coherent images of an object from novel viewpoints given only one reference image. Recent diffusion-based approaches have substantially improved the realism and efficiency of multi-view synthesis [ 39 , 33 , 31 , 8 , 29 , 27 , 43 , 25 , 4 , 7 ] by leveraging large-scale image priors and joint view generation [ 37 , 28 , 21 , 38 , 16 , 44 ] . Nevertheless, a single reference image provides only partial observations of the underlying object. The geometry of occluded and unseen regions therefore remains underconstrained, making it difficult to preserve plausible object structure and multi-view consistent local appearance. To reduce this ambiguity, geometry-guided methods [ 19 , 20 , 26 , 15 , 6 , 13 , 42 ] introduce normal maps, depth maps, or other structural representations as explicit conditions for multi-view RGB synthesis. When the geometry condition is accurate, it provides view-aware structural cues that help constrain object shape and appearance in unseen regions. Figure 1 (a,b) highlights two alternative formulations for multi-view generation. Direct methods do not expose geometry as an independently controllable signal, whereas geometry-guided pipelines expose it without accounting for its non-uniform reliability. However, geometry predicted from a single reference image is not uniformly reliable. Ambiguity in occluded regions, thin structures, and local boundaries can lead to spatially and view-wise varying errors in the predicted geometry. Existing geometry-conditioned pipelines [ 45 , 25 , 19 , 20 , 26 ] typically inject predicted geometry with a globally fixed strength, implicitly treating all geometric cues as equally trustworthy. This design creates an unavoidable trade-off that weak conditioning underuses reliable geometry, whereas strong conditioning propagates local geometric errors into RGB synthesis. Because the reliability of predicted geometry varies across spatial locations and target views, no single global injection scale can simultaneously preserve trustworthy structural cues and suppress unreliable ones. This limitation motivates a selective geometry-conditioning mechanism that preserves stable geometric cues while suppressing unreliable ones. Figure 1 : Comparison of three paradigms for multi-view image generation. (a) Direct generation entangles geometric reasoning and texture synthesis in a single generator, making geometric errors difficult to isolate. (b) Geometry-guided generation separates geometry prediction from RGB synthesis, but applies predicted geometry with spatially uniform influence. (c) RGMV conditions RGB synthesis on an anchor geometry prediction and uses per-view spatial reliability maps estimated by SCG to modulate geometry residuals through RGI. Therefore, we propose RGMV, a reliability-guided framework for geometry-guided multi-view generation. Figure 1 (c) summarizes the resulting alternative. RGMV retains the decoupled pipeline but selectively controls the influence of predicted geometry rather than modifying the geometry itself. RGMV obtains multiple normal predictions for the same reference image and target poses from a geometry proposal generator under different stochastic seeds. SCG converts their agreement into spatial reliability maps, and RGI uses these maps to modulate the geometry residuals injected into the multi-view RGB synthesis model. This design preserves stronger geometry guidance in stable regions while limiting the influence of inconsistent predictions. Experiments show that SCG-guided RGI improves over spatially uniform injection with a frozen RGB synthesis model, and parameter-efficient adaptation further improves the full RGMV framework. The main contributions of this work are as follows: • We propose RGMV, which couples a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) for estimating spatial reliability from stochastic geometry agreement with a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module for modulating normal-conditioned residuals. • We introduce a parameter-efficient adaptation scheme for the RGI-equipped RGB synthesis model, which uses ground-truth normals during training and SCG-derived spatial variation only at inference, without dependence on a particular geometry proposal generator. • Extensive experiments on Objaverse and GSO demonstrate that RGMV consistently improves multiple geometry proposal generators in both multi-view RGB synthesis and downstream 3D reconstruction. Qualitative results show more stable structures on rendered objects and real captured images. 2 Related Work 2.1 Multi-view Consistent Image Generation Diffusion-based models [ 17 , 32 , 18 , 33 , 36 , 35 ] have become a major approach for synthesizing novel views from a single reference image. Zero-1-to-3 [ 17 ] introduces camera-conditioned diffusion, enabling novel-view generation under specified relative camera transformations. SyncDreamer [ 18 ] further models the joint distribution of multiple target views and synchronizes their denoising process through cross-view feature interaction to improve multi-view consistency. SV3D [ 36 ] adapts latent video diffusion to orbital multi-view synthesis and incorporates explicit camera control for image-conditioned view generation. Era3D [ 14 ] improves high-resolution multi-view generation through camera prediction and efficient row-wise attention that exploits epipolar correspondence across views. More recently, MV-Adapter [ 10 ] introduces a lightweight adapter-based design that equips pretrained text-to-image diffusion models with multi-view generation capability while preserving the original backbone. These methods [ 35 , 34 , 47 , 7 , 1 ] improve the realism, camera controllability, and cross-view coherence of image-based multi-view synthesis. Their primary focus is on constructing stronger multi-view generation priors or more effective cross-view interactions. In this work, we study how external geometry predicted from a single reference image should be used within an existing multi-view diffusion pipeline when the reliability varies across spatial regions and target views. 2.2 Geometry-conditioned Diffusion Models Geometry conditions have been widely used to provide explicit spatial control for diffusion models [ 45 , 25 , 43 , 9 , 22 , 40 , 24 , 2 ] . ControlNet [ 45 ] introduces an additional trainable branch that injects spatial conditions, such as edges, depth maps, and normal maps, into a pretrained diffusion backbone. T2I-Adapter [ 25 ] instead learns lightweight adapters for external structural signals while keeping the original text-to-image model frozen. These methods establish effective mechanisms for incorporating geometry into image diffusion. Several works further incorporate geometry into multi-view or 3D generation [ 19 , 20 , 6 , 13 , 15 ] . Wonder3D [ 19 ] jointly generates multi-view RGB images and normal maps through cross-domain diffusion and multi-view cross-domain attention. Direct2.5 [ 20 ] models multi-view normal maps as a 2.5D representation and uses normal-conditioned multi-view image generation for appearance synthesis. PointmapDiff [ 26 ] uses predicted pointmaps as geometric conditions for single-image novel-view synthesis through reference attention and ControlNet-based conditioning. In a related texture-generation setting, CaliTex [ 15 ] calibrates attention with known 3D structure to improve view-coherent texture synthesis. These methods demonstrate that explicit geometry can substantially improve view synthesis and appearance generation. However, they generally use the available geometric representation directly or condition generation with a globally fixed mechanism [ 45 , 19 , 20 , 26 ] . Regarding this issue, RGMV uses multi-sample agreement to adapt the strength of geometry-conditioned residual injection at inference time. 2.3 Consistency-based Reliability Estimation Multi-sample consistency has been explored as an inference-time signal for assessing the reliability of generative outputs [ 23 , 12 , 11 ] . Generative Uncertainty in Diffusion Models [ 12 ] estimates the uncertainty of diffusion samples to identify potentially low-quality generations. Self-Refining Video Sampling [ 11 ] uses self-consistency to identify regions that benefit from selective refinement during video generation. These studies show that repeated stochastic generations can provide useful evidence about output stability without requiring an additional manually annotated reliability label. RGMV evaluates the stability of the geometry condition before it is injected into downstream multi-view RGB synthesis. Specifically, SCG measures agreement among normal predictions generated under different stochastic seeds and converts it into a spatial reliability map. This parameter-free signal directly modulates normal-conditioned residuals at inference time, allowing the multi-view diffusion model to retain stable geometric cues while attenuating geometry conditions that are locally inconsistent. Figure 2 : Overview of RGMV. Given a reference image and target camera poses, an off-the-shelf geometry proposal generator produces K K stochastic sets of multi-view normal predictions. The first prediction set serves as the anchor normal condition to produce multi-level geometry residuals. In parallel, Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) in (a) groups normal predictions by target view, measures their per-pixel angular disagreement, and converts it into per-view spatial reliability maps. Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module in (b) resizes and affinely calibrates the corresponding reliability map at each denoising level l l to obtain 𝐑 ~ v , l \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}_{v,l} , which selectively modulates the geometry residual before it is injected into the multi-view diffusion backbone. 3 Method 3.1 Overview Given a reference image 𝐈 ref \mathbf{I}_{\mathrm{ref}} and a set of target camera poses 𝒫 = { 𝐏 v } v = 1 V \mathcal{P}=\left\{\mathbf{P}_{v}\right\}_{v=1}^{V} , our goal is to synthesize a set of multi-view RGB images ℐ ^ = { 𝐈 ^ v } v = 1 V \hat{\mathcal{I}}=\left\{\hat{\mathbf{I}}_{v}\right\}_{v=1}^{V} that are consistent with the reference appearance and the target viewpoints. In this work, we instantiate the geometry representation with multi-view normal maps.
